==English==
{{wp}}

===Etymology 1===
From {{inh|en|enm|none}}, {{m|enm|noon}}, {{m|enm|non|t=not one}}, from {{inh|en|ang|nān|t=not one, not any, none}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*nain}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*nainaz|t=none, nought, nothing}}, equivalent to {{af|en|ne|t1=not|one|nocat=1}}. (Regarding the different phonological development of ''only'' and ''one'', see the note in {{m|en|one}}.)

Cognate with {{cog|sco|nane|t=none}}, {{cog|stq|naan}}, {{m|stq|neen|t=no, not any, none}}, {{cog|fy|neen}} & {{m|fy|gjin|t=no, none}}, {{cog|nl|neen}} & {{m|nl|geen|t=no, none}}, {{cog|nds|nen|nēn}}, {{m|nds|neen}}, {{m|nds|keen|t=no, none, no one}}, {{cog|de|nein}} & {{m|de|kein|t=no, none}}, {{cog|la|nōn||not}}.

====Alternative forms====
* {{alter|en|non}} {{defdate|11th|17th c.}}

====Pronunciation====
* {{IPA|en|/nʌn/|[nʌn ~ nɐn]|a=RP,GA,CA}}

** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Grendelkhan-none.wav|a=Connecticut|IPA=[nɐn]}}
** {{audio|en|en-us-none.ogg|a=California|IPA=[nɐ̃n]}}
* {{IPA|en|/nɐn/|[nɐn ~ nän]|a=AU,NZ}}
* {{IPA|en|/nʊn/|a=North England,Dublin}}
* {{IPA|en|/nɔn/|a=UK,dialectal}}
* {{homophones|en|nun}}
* {{rhymes|en|ʌn|s=1}}

====Pronoun====
{{en-pron}}
[[File:Similar-geometric-shapes-all-illustration.svg|thumb|In this picture, '''none''' of the blue shapes are inside the yellow boundary.]]

# [[not|Not]] [[any]] of a [[given]] [[number]] or [[group]].
#: {{ux|en|'''None''' of those is a good example. '''None''' are even acceptable.}}
#: {{ux|en|'''None''' of this meat tastes right.}}
#: {{ux|en|There were many but now there are '''none'''.}} 
## [[no one|No one]], [[nobody]].
##: {{ux|en|'''None''' of those people is my father.}}
## [[no|No]] [[person]].
##: {{ux|en|'''None''' of those people are my parents. '''None''' shall pass.
}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=2006|author=w:Clive James|title=North Face of Soho|page=253
|passage=Alas, '''none''' of these people were writing the reviews.}}

=====Usage notes=====
* ''None'' used to replace [[w:uncountable noun|uncountable noun]]s should always be singular. ''None'' used in place of [[w:countable noun|countable noun]]s may be either singular or plural, unless the rest of the circumstances or phrasing require it to be one or the other.

=====Antonyms=====
* {{l|en|some}}
* {{l|en|all}}

====Determiner====
{{en-head|det}}

# {{lb|en|archaic|outside|Scotland|West Country}} Not any; [[no]] (usually used only before a vowel or ''h'').
#: {{ux|en|Thou shalt have '''none''' other gods but me.}}
#* {{RQ:Tyndale NT|Matthew|XXV|text=the foles toke their lampes, but toke '''none''' oyle with them.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2008|author=w:James Kelman|title=Kieron Smith, Boy|page=138|publisher=Penguin|year_published=2009
|passage='''None''' lasses were in the dunces' row. If one had been there people would have looked at her and felt sorry but not boys.}}

====Adverb====
{{en-adv|-}}

# {{senseid|en|in no way}} To no extent, in no way. {{defdate|from 11th c.}}
#: {{ux|en|I felt [[none the|'''none''' the]] worse for my recent illness.}}
#* {{quote-song|en|year=1973|author=w:Paul Simon|title={{w|Kodachrome (song)|Kodachrome}}|passage=my lack of education hasn't hurt me '''none'''}}
# Not at all, not very. {{defdate|from 13th c.}}
#: {{ux|en|He was '''none''' too pleased with the delays in the program that was supposed to be his legacy.}}
#: {{ux|en|We could hear '''none''' too well from the back.}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} [[no|No]], [[not]]. {{defdate|14th|16th c.}}

===Etymology 2===
From the first sense, since they respond “none” when asked about their religion; also a play on words on {{m|en|nun}}.

====Pronunciation====
* {{IPA|en|/nʌn/|/nɒn/}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-none.ogg|a=US}}
* {{rhymes|en|ʌn|ɒn|s=1}}
* {{homophones|en|nun|non-}}

====Noun====
{{en-noun}}

# {{lb|en|chiefly|American}} A person without religious affiliation.
#* {{RQ:NYT|title=America’s Very Weird Religious Future|author=Ross Douthat|quotee={{w|Ryan Burge (political scientist)|Ryan Burge}}|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/01/22/opinion/interesting-times-ryan-burge.html|date=Jan. 22, 2026|passage=
So the “'''nones'''” are those three groups together: atheist, agnostic, nothing in particular. That group has grown from 5 percent of America in 1972 to about 30 percent of America today.|archiveurl=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/6CCDK|archivedate=25 February 2026}}

===Etymology 3===
From {{der|en|fr|none}}, from {{der|en|la|nōna|t=[[ninth]]; [[ninth]] [[hour]]}}.<ref>[http://www.oed.com/view/Entry/127903 "none, ''n.''"], in the ''Oxford English Dictionary'', Oxford: Oxford University Press.</ref>

====Pronunciation====
* {{IPA|en|/nəʊn/|a=UK}}
* {{IPA|en|/noʊn/|a=US}}
* {{rhymes|en|əʊn|oʊn|s=1}}
* {{homophone|en|known}}

====Noun====
{{en-noun}}

# {{alt form|en|nones}}: the [[ninth]] [[hour]] after [[dawn]]; {{lb|en|Christian}} the [[religious]] [[service]] [[appoint]]ed to [[this]] [[hour]].
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} {{syn of|en|midafternoon}}: the [[time]] [[around]] or [[follow]]ing [[noon]] or [[nones]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1706|translator=D. Cotes|author=L.E. Dupin|title=A New Ecclesiastical History of the 16th Century|volume=II|chapter=v, 43
|passage=The last, which began at the middle of the Afternoon, i.e. at half the Time between Noon and Sun-setting, was called '''None''', because it began at the Ninth Hour.}}
